rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Gas equilibria speak two dialects — concentrations and partial pressures — and **Kp = Kc(RT)^Δn** is the dictionary. The derivation is one ideal-gas line: p = [i]RT turns every pressure into a concentration, and collecting the leftover RT factors leaves (RT) raised to Δn, the change in **gaseous** moles between products and reactants.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - p_i = [i]RT - Kp = (pC)^c(pD)^d / (pA)^a(pB)^b - Kp = Kc(RT)^Δn; Kc = Kp/(RT)^Δn - Δn = Σ gas moles (products) − Σ gas moles (reactants) - Worked: Kc = 0.16, T = 300 K, Δn = +1 → Kp = 3.94

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ All cells look the same under a microscope. ✅ Prokaryotic cells lack membrane-bound organelles; eukaryotic cells have them.  ·  ❌ DNA and RNA are identical in structure. ✅ DNA is double-stranded with deoxyribose and thymine; RNA is single-stranded with ribose and uracil.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***The ammonia check*** — Kc = 0.061 at 500 K for N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃: dividing by (0.0821 × 500)² ≈ 1681 gives Kp ≈ 3.6 × 10⁻⁵ — four orders smaller, because four gas moles collapse into two.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: ❌ Mitosis produces genetically different cells. ✅ Mitosis produces genetically identical diploid daughter cells.  ·  ❌ Meiosis produces identical cells. ✅ Meiosis produces 4 genetically diverse haploid gametes.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Count gas moles first: Δn = 0 → answer "Kp = Kc" instantly. Bridge ladder: +1 → ×RT; −1 → ÷RT; −2 → ÷(RT)². Kelvin conversion: °C + 273.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB-style (3m): Derive the relationship between Kp and Kc for a gaseous reaction.** — Consider aA(g) + bB(g) ⇌ cC(g) + dD(g). By the ideal gas law, the partial pressure of any gaseous component is p_i = n_iRT/V = [i]RT, where [i] is its molar concentration. The pressure-based equilibrium constant is Kp = (pC)^c(pD)^d / (pA)^a(pB)^b.…  ·  **NEB-style (2m): For which reaction is Kp = Kc: (a) N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g), (b) H₂(g) + I₂(g) ⇌ 2HI(g), (c) N₂O₄(g) ⇌ 2NO₂(g)? Compute Δn for each.** — **(a)** Δn = (2) − (1 + 3) = −2; Kp = Kc(RT)⁻² = Kc/(RT)², so Kp < Kc.…

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: In derivations, state p = [i]RT explicitly — that single ideal-gas line is where the (RT)^Δn factor comes from, and examiners look for it.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: One sign decides everything: Δn. Zero means the two constants are twins; positive makes Kp larger; negative makes Kc larger — read the balanced equation before touching the calculator.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Partial pressure = CRT (ideal gas) - pressures are concentrations in disguise. Kp = (pC)^c(pD)^d/(pA)^a(pB)^b. Bridge: Kp = Kc(RT)^dn, dn = gas moles products - reactants; T in kelvin; R matches pressure unit. dn = 0: Kp = Kc (HI). dn = +1: Kp = Kc(RT) (N2O4, PCl5). dn = -2: Kp = Kc/(RT)2 (NH3). Units atm^dn.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: High-altitude physiology and pressure cookers both live on p = CRT: the same relation that turns concentrations into partial pressures governs how thin air and sealed steam behave.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: **NEB-style (2m numerical): For N₂O₄(g) ⇌ 2NO₂(g), Kc = 0.16 at 300 K. Calculate Kp (R = 0.0821 L atm mol⁻¹ K⁻¹).** — Δn = 2 − 1 = +1, so Kp = Kc(RT)^1 = 0.16 × 0.0821 × 300. Multiplying: 0.0821 × 300 = 24.63; 0.16 × 24.63 ≈ **3.94**. Since Δn = +1, Kp carries the units of pressure (atm¹).…

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Two Constants, One Reaction, One Bridge Gas-phase equilibria can be written in concentrations (Kc) or in partial pressures (Kp). The two are not rivals but conversions of the same fact, and **Kp = Kc(RT)^Δn** is the bridge — where Δn is the change in gas moles and T is absolute temperature.…  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Kp — the pressure-side constant - For gas reactions, the active mass of each gas is proportional to its **partial pressure** (from the ideal gas law: pV = nRT → p = (n/V)RT = CRT). - For aA(g) + bB(g) ⇌ cC(g) + dD(g): **Kp = (pC)^c(pD)^d / (pA)^a(pB)^b** — partial pressures replacing concentrations.…  ·  ## 3. rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ Crossing over occurs in mitosis. ✅ Crossing over occurs in Prophase I of meiosis only.  ·  ❌ All enzymes are proteins. ✅ Most enzymes are proteins; some RNA molecules (ribozymes) also have catalytic activity.  ·  ❌ ATP is the only energy currency. ✅ GTP, UTP, and CTP also serve as energy carriers in specific pathways.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ Photosynthesis occurs in all plant cells. ✅ Photosynthesis occurs only in cells containing chloroplasts (mainly mesophyll).  ·  ❌ Respiration and photosynthesis are opposite processes with same equation. ✅ They are complementary but occur in different organelles and under different conditions.  ·  ❌ Oxygen is produced during respiration. ✅ Oxygen is consumed in aerobic respiration; produced during photosynthesis.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ Food chain shows all feeding relationships. ✅ Food chain is linear; food web shows interconnected feeding relationships.  ·  ❌ 90% of energy is transferred to next trophic level. ✅ Only ~10% energy transfers; ~90% lost as heat.  ·  ❌ Biomagnification decreases toxin concentration up the food chain. ✅ Biomagnification increases toxin concentration at higher trophic levels.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ Carbon cycle only involves plants and animals. ✅ Carbon cycle involves atmosphere, oceans, fossils, rocks, and decomposers.  ·  ❌ Nitrogen fixation only occurs in bacteria. ✅ Some lightning and industrial processes (Haber) also fix nitrogen.  ·  ❌ All fungi are harmful. ✅ Many fungi are beneficial (decomposers, mycorrhizae, food, antibiotics like penicillin).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ Viruses are living organisms. ✅ Viruses are acellular — they cannot reproduce without a host and lack metabolism.  ·  ❌ Bacteria are always harmful. ✅ Most bacteria are harmless or beneficial (gut flora, nitrogen fixation, decomposition).  ·  ❌ Gram-positive and Gram-negative differ only in color. ✅ Gram-positive has thick peptidoglycan layer; Gram-negative has thin layer + outer membrane.
